name: Cognition
tagline: Makers of Devin (an autonomous AI software engineer) and owners of Windsurf (an AI IDE, acquired 2025). Little first-hand loop data is public: the CEO describes the main engineering interview as building your own end-to-end coding agent in roughly 6–8 hours, and third-party guides describe a recruiter call, a practical live-coding screen and an in-person SF onsite.
notes: Very few candidate-reported questions are public, so every problem here is written IN THE STYLE OF what is reported. None of them is a confirmed Cognition question. What is reported: CEO Scott Wu has said the interview has people 'build their own Devin in eight hours, and see how far they get', meaning a full end-to-end agent, and that high-level decision making matters more than language syntax. Third-party guides (not first-hand) describe a practical, pair-programming-style coding screen, sometimes in an unfamiliar language or library with docs allowed, and a product-flavored systems round (e.g. the sandbox an agent runs in). For the Windsurf/Codeium side, before the acquisition: a 2025 Glassdoor report describes a 45-minute round about building a search engine; another describes an AI-allowed OA plus two medium/medium-hard DS&A rounds; a 1point3acres thread describes a Codeium OA on file replication in Python. The problems here practice the pieces of a coding agent and a dev tool: the file-editing tool an agent calls, applying a model-generated patch, code search, and directory sync. Expect interviewers to care about getting a working end-to-end thing quickly, precise and model-friendly tool I/O, edge cases, and clear trade-off decisions.
